---

```{r}
raw %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  filter(!is.na(weight_kg)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(body_length_cm, weight_kg)) +
  geom_point()

# five lines instead of fifty
```

Is your script dozens of lines that repeat the same thing? Not sure what a pipeline is, or how `mutate()` and `map()` work? After this workshop, that is in the past.

We work with one dataset the whole day: messy capture records of big cats, from first import to finished plots.

## What you will learn

1. Tidyverse and how pipelines work
2. Importing and cleaning data, NA values and outliers
3. Transforming data: `filter()`, `mutate()`, `summarise()`, joins
4. Visualisation with `ggplot2` and facets, with a short introduction to interactive plots in `plotly`
5. Iteration with loops and without: `for()`, `lapply()` `map()` from `purrr`
6. Troubleshooting and tips for everyday work

## Who it is for

Students and researchers who already work in RStudio. No need to write your own functions, just basic familiarity with R and the motivation to learn something new.

Stuck on your own data? Let us know in advance at [kadleci@fzp.czu.cz](mailto:kadleci@fzp.czu.cz), and if it does not fit in the workshop, we will look at it over a glass of good wine in the evening!

## Before the workshop

Please bring your own laptop and prepare it **before** the workshop. Installing everything on site takes a lot of time and the Wi-Fi may be slow.

### 1. Install the software

| Software | Version | Download |
|---|---|---|
| R | 4.5.0 or newer | <https://cran.r-project.org/> |
| RStudio Desktop | latest | <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/> |
| Rtools (Windows only) | matching your R version | <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/> |

Already have R? Check your version in the RStudio console:

```{r}
R.version.string
```

### 2. Install the packages

Run this once in the RStudio console:

```{r}
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse",   # dplyr, tidyr, readr, stringr, ggplot2, purrr, lubridate
  "janitor",     # clean_names()
  "writexl",     # export to Excel
  "here",        # file paths in projects
  "plotly",      # interactive plots
  "htmlwidgets", # save interactive plots as HTML
  "pkgbuild"     # check Rtools on Windows
))
```

### 3. Test that everything works

Copy the whole block into the console and run it:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(plotly)

# Versions
R.version.string
packageVersion("tidyverse")

# Windows only: is Rtools installed?
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)

# A small test with built-in data
test <- iris %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_length = mean(sepal_length))

test

# A plot and its interactive version
p <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point()

p
ggplotly(p)

# Iteration with purrr
1:3 %>% map_dbl(\(x) x * 2)
```

If everything works, you should see:

- a table with 3 species and their mean sepal length
- a scatter plot in the Plots pane
- the same plot as an interactive version in the Viewer pane
- the numbers `2 4 6`

**Something does not work?** Copy the error message and send it to [kadleci@fzp.czu.cz](mailto:kadleci@fzp.czu.cz) before the workshop, we will help you fix it.

### 4. Download the workshop materials

All scripts and data will be available on GitHub on **Tuesday 24 November in the evening**: <https://github.com/kadleci/Workshop-Less-Code-More-results>

Click **Code > Download ZIP**, unzip the folder and open the `.Rproj` file in RStudio.
